speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and has it spread since it first appeared? Also, are you experiencing any joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash have a characteristic "slapped cheek" appearance, and have you noticed any joint pain or swelling in your hands or knees? I would also like to check if the rash on your limbs is lacy or reticular in pattern.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation is classic for Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum
